sonnet.q1: They do not differ. Both get HTTP 401 and the login page showing "Invalid email or password", with the same body and matched timing (a dummy bcrypt compare is run when no user matches).
sonnet.q2: The email is locked: the login is refused with HTTP 429 (login page with Retry-After) without checking the password and without any bcrypt call. The lock lasts 15 minutes. The 5th failure itself also returns 429 and sets the lock.
sonnet.q3: The login always creates a brand-new session ID. In the same transaction, the session row matching the hash of the incoming cookie is deleted (zero rows matched is fine). A malformed cookie is treated as no cookie. The new cookie is sent only after commit.
sonnet.q4: Only the opaque random session ID (43-character base64url, 32 random bytes), with no user data. Page scripts cannot read it because the cookie is HttpOnly (also Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, named __Host-sid).
sonnet.q5: At 12 hours after login. Expires_at is login plus 12 hours and is never extended. Continuous use keeps the 30-minute idle clock restarting, so the 12-hour cap is what ends it.
sonnet.q6: It responds with a 303 redirect to /login and clears (expires) the cookie. A missing or malformed cookie gets the same redirect with cookie expiry, without a database call.
sonnet.q7: With a well-formed cookie, the server DELETEs the session row (matched by the SHA-256 hash of the ID) before replying, then sends a 303 to /login with the cookie expired. If the session is already gone, the delete removes 0 rows and the result is the same. With no or malformed cookie, no database call is made and it redirects to /login with cookie expiry. On a database error or timeout it returns a 503 and keeps the cookie.
sonnet.q8: In the shared Postgres database, in the sessions table (keyed by the SHA-256 hex of the session ID). Each request's cookie value is hashed by the app and looked up by primary key, so any instance can serve any request and no sticky sessions are needed.
sonnet.q9: In the Postgres login_throttle table, one row per normalized (trimmed, lowercase) email, with a failed_at timestamptz[] list and locked_until. On each checked failure, the app appends the failure time and drops every timestamp older than 10 minutes, using a single clock_timestamp() read from the database clock taken after the row lock is held. It then counts what remains, including the current attempt.
sonnet.q10: The app hashes the cookie value (SHA-256 hex) and the single UPDATE compares it to the id_hash primary key. It also checks that last_seen_at is later than now minus 30 minutes and expires_at is later than now, and joins users. If a row matches, it writes last_seen_at = now() and returns the user id and email.
sonnet.q11: A 503 page (sign-in temporarily unavailable, try again shortly) with no cookie set. The transaction is rolled back and the attempt is not counted.
sonnet.q12: The sweep job. Each app instance runs a timer every 10 minutes and takes a Postgres advisory lock so only one sweeps at a time. It deletes sessions where expires_at is past or last_seen_at is over 30 minutes old (and dead throttle rows).
